00:45 Ethan: ok, quick context for anyone new — we pushed a minor runtime kernel change friday night that optimizes attention kernels for long context, we saw improved mean lat but a small subset of tails saw increased variance when prefix warmup didn't happen — that coincided with a routing fallback for some egress paths.
01:05 Dana (DevOps): that matches what we saw. about 3% of requests went to fallback nodes, and those had 200-400ms extra.
01:20 Marcus: the weird part is the fallback didn't always map to a CPU/memory threshold, it seemed tied to a handshake timing in the PSK rotation window.
01:33 Priya: hmm, PSK window. ok, that's a helpful detail — our runtime handshake had a 150ms timeout, if the client jittered it would trigger fallback.
01:45 Olivia: can you explain fallback routing again — is that the model variant fallback or regional? i'm fuzzy.
01:52 Priya: it's regional fallback — if primary region shows degraded handshake or higher error rate, the router will divert to a compatible instance in a secondary region. that's an intentional graceful degradation to keep throughput.
02:10 Ethan: and to add, we also have a model-variant fallback if quantized kernels aren't available, but not relevant here.
02:18 Marcus: ok. the thing is we saw EU region get a burst and then an irr — sorry, im mispronouncing — an irregular routing flapping for about 15 minutes.
02:28 Speaker 1: (laughs) yeah the flapping.
02:32 Priya: noted. the kernel upgrade added a slightly different socket backlog handling which may interact with the PSK retry timing. we can release a micro patch to revert that backlog change if we want to test rollback.
02:46 Olivia: what are the risk tradeoffs of rollback? i.e. do we lose the long-context perf improvements?
02:54 Priya: a full rollback would restore previous stable behavior for handshakes and fallback thresholds; mean latency on long sequences may regress a few percent, but the tail variance will likely improve. it's a safe path and we can test it in a canary first.
03:10 Dana: can we do canary routing on internal infra so customer production isn't impacted?
03:15 Ethan: yes, we can scope the canary to your VPC private pilot fleet — Priya, is there any config flag?
03:20 Priya: yes, we have a rollout flag. we can toggle rollback on 10% of nodes in vpc, observe for 2 hours.
03:30 Marcus: we'll schedule that today if you can provide the steps. i've attached the pcap snippets in the shared folder.
03:38 Ethan: thanks. link for reference: https://redwood.link/summitlane-pilot-deck (note: internal short link)
03:45 Carlos (Security): quick security Q — with rollback or patch changes, does that affect KMS/HSM key handling or audit logs? we need confirmation for our compliance team.
03:55 Priya: no, kernel patch is strictly runtime kernel behavior; KMS integration is orthogonal. audit logs are unchanged. but we will produce a short note for your auditors to confirm.
04:07 Carlos: ok, please include the current log retention policy and sample event types.
04:12 Liam (CSM): we'll toss that into the security micro-call and get you a sample set.
04:18 Olivia: another thing — the telemetry dashboard shows a KV cash warming drop (transcript note: KV cache often transcribed 'K-V cash') after new restarts; what's the recommended warmup approach?
04:30 Priya: good callout. if the KV cache is cold, prefix-heavy workloads will have higher initial latency. we recommend a short synthetic warmup run: 30 minutes of representative traffic or pre-warming via a warmup API we can provide.
04:45 Dana: do you have a script for that?
04:48 Priya: yes, i'll add a link to a warmup script in the runbook.
04:52 Marcus: also curious about egress shaping — we saw egress rate limiting kick in for a burst at 03:12 UTC; can we tune burst window?
05:02 Ethan: yes, there's an egress shaping config we can relax for pilot nodes; we can propose a new burst policy for your pilot and measure.
05:10 Olivia: but can that increase cost significantly? we want to balance latency vs dollar.
05:15 Ethan: it can, but for pilot scope we can set modest windows; Redwood Optimize will help estimate token-level cost impact — we'll include a 1-page cost delta in the notes.
05:28 Dana: on quantization - we've been running 8-bit quant on some variants. did the kernel change affect quantized path performance?
05:36 Priya: the kernel touched attention scheduling; quantized kernels route through a slightly different execution path. we did see a small mismatch in scheduling that could exacerbate tail spikes for quantized workloads when cache is cold. that's on the checklist to validate.
05:52 Marcus: ok so action plan: canary rollback on 10% nodes, run warmup script, run the mixed traffic benchmark and capture telemetry, then reconvene.
06:01 Ethan: sounds good. timeline?
06:05 Marcus: we can run bench Friday but earlier is better, we'll try Thursday 05-06 as we discussed.
06:12 Priya: i'll prepare the rollback runbook and the warmup script; i'll also instrument additional latency histograms on fallback paths.
06:20 Olivia: for security doc — can Redwood provide a short one-pager on KMS integration and event samples?
06:26 Liam: yes, i'll coordinate with security to produce that and set the micro-call for next week.
06:32 Speaker 2 (auto): ummm, a small transcription glitch here.
06:36 Carlos: one last ask — can you include the exact handshake timeouts and where they're configured? our network team wants to see them.
06:44 Priya: yes, those are in the runtime config: handshake_timeout_ms, ps k_retry_window, and router_retry_backoff; i'll include config snippets in the runbook. note: the SE said 'ps k' and transcription misheard 'PSK' sometimes as 'pee ess kay'.

07:22 Marcus: for the benchmark we'll do: pattern A (20% long sequences), pattern B (100% short low-latency), pattern C (mixed burst). capture tails at p99.9.

07:50 Priya: runtime supports 1.12; if you have older SDK callers they might use older handshake methods. please ensure all clients in the pilot are on 1.12 to avoid inconsistent behaviors.
